question: A collection utility is setting its level of service targets for the year. Which input most directly shapes the cleaning and inspection targets that follow?
correctAnswer: The condition and criticality ratings assigned to each sewer segment
explanation: Cleaning and inspection effort follows risk, so segment condition and criticality ratings set the targets. Fleet age, painting counts, and camera preference do not measure sewer risk.
options: The age of the oldest jetting truck in the maintenance yard fleet
The condition and criticality ratings assigned to each sewer segment
The number of manholes repainted during the previous field season
The camera model preferred by the closed circuit inspection crew
optionA: The age of the oldest jetting truck in the maintenance yard fleet
optionB: The condition and criticality ratings assigned to each sewer segment
optionC: The number of manholes repainted during the previous field season
optionD: The camera model preferred by the closed circuit inspection crew
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: During a wet weather study, monitored flow rises sharply within minutes of rainfall starting and falls soon after rain ends. Which inflow source does that pattern point to?
correctAnswer: Roof leaders or foundation drains connected directly to the sanitary sewer
explanation: A rapid rise and fall that tracks rainfall points to direct inflow connections such as roof leaders and foundation drains. Groundwater infiltration responds slowly and persists after rain ends.
options: Roof leaders or foundation drains connected directly to the sanitary sewer
Groundwater seeping slowly through cracked pipe joints over several weeks
Backflow entering from the treatment plant through the outfall sewer line
Leakage from a pressurized watermain crossing above the sanitary sewer
optionA: Roof leaders or foundation drains connected directly to the sanitary sewer
optionB: Groundwater seeping slowly through cracked pipe joints over several weeks
optionC: Backflow entering from the treatment plant through the outfall sewer line
optionD: Leakage from a pressurized watermain crossing above the sanitary sewer

question: Odour complaints cluster at the manhole where a force main discharges into a gravity sewer. Which condition at that point most often drives the odour release?
correctAnswer: Turbulent discharge strips hydrogen sulfide from the sewage into the air
explanation: Sulfide builds up in the force main, and turbulence at the discharge strips hydrogen sulfide into the air space, causing the complaints. Calm flow and cold sewage do not release gas the same way.
options: Cold sewage in the gravity sewer absorbs odours from the air above it
Smooth laminar flow in the receiving sewer releases dissolved gases
Turbulent discharge strips hydrogen sulfide from the sewage into the air
Chlorine residual in the sewage reacts with the manhole benching
optionA: Cold sewage in the gravity sewer absorbs odours from the air above it
optionB: Smooth laminar flow in the receiving sewer releases dissolved gases
optionC: Turbulent discharge strips hydrogen sulfide from the sewage into the air
optionD: Chlorine residual in the sewage reacts with the manhole benching
sourceTitle: Canadian Centre for Occupational Health and Safety - Hydrogen Sulfide

Remove one duty pump from service to reduce wear until the upgrade funding arrives

question: Pressure logging on a force main shows transients well above the normal operating range after pump stops. Which action comes first?
correctAnswer: Review pump control and surge protection, and inspect the air valves along the profile
explanation: Surge transients call for checking pump control, surge devices, and air valves before replacing pipe. Higher speeds and parallel full speed operation can worsen the transients.
options: Increase pump speed so the main stays pressurized for longer periods during each day
Replace the lowest section of pipe before checking the cause of the pressure transients
Review pump control and surge protection, and inspect the air valves along the profile
Add a second discharge header so both pumps can run together at full speed every cycle
optionA: Increase pump speed so the main stays pressurized for longer periods during each day
optionB: Replace the lowest section of pipe before checking the cause of the pressure transients
optionC: Review pump control and surge protection, and inspect the air valves along the profile

Sealing every manhole cover along the trunk route to keep the gases inside the sewer
Scheduling complaint responses for early morning, when fewer residents are outdoors

question: Run time records show one pump at a duplex station doing most of the work while its twin sits largely unused. Which strategy balances the asset risk?
correctAnswer: Alternate the duty assignment regularly and track run hours so wear stays balanced
explanation: Alternating duty balances wear and keeps the standby pump proven and ready. Running one pump to failure, lag pumping every cycle, or storing the spare all raise risk.
options: Keep the stronger pump as the permanent duty unit until it reaches its end of life
Run both pumps together on every cycle so the wet well empties as fast as possible
Remove the spare pump into storage so it stays new until the duty pump finally fails
Alternate the duty assignment regularly and track run hours so wear stays balanced

optionB: Run both pumps together on every cycle so the wet well empties as fast as possible
optionC: Remove the spare pump into storage so it stays new until the duty pump finally fails

question: A force main has no isolation valves along its river crossing section. Which risk does that gap create for the renewal plan?
correctAnswer: A failure there forces a long shutdown and a difficult emergency repair
explanation: Without isolation valves, a crossing failure cannot be isolated, so repair means a long shutdown under difficult conditions. Friction, air release, and pump cycling are separate issues.
options: A failure there forces a long shutdown and a difficult emergency repair
The main will run at higher pressure because valves add friction losses
Air will collect at the crossing because valves are needed to release it
The pumps will cycle more often because the wet well drains back fully
optionA: A failure there forces a long shutdown and a difficult emergency repair
optionB: The main will run at higher pressure because valves add friction losses
optionC: Air will collect at the crossing because valves are needed to release it
optionD: The pumps will cycle more often because the wet well drains back fully

question: Concrete corrosion is found at the crown of a trunk sewer, while the walls below the waterline look sound. Which explanation fits that pattern?
correctAnswer: Hydrogen sulfide released above the waterline is converted to acid on the crown
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide escapes into the air space and is converted to sulfuric acid on the moist crown, attacking concrete above the waterline. Scouring, groundwater, and grease do not produce that pattern.
options: Sewage flowing at high velocity scours the crown more than the lower pipe walls
Groundwater pressure outside the pipe dissolves the crown from the outside inward
Hydrogen sulfide released above the waterline is converted to acid on the crown
Grease deposits floating on the surface protect the crown and attack the walls
optionA: Sewage flowing at high velocity scours the crown more than the lower pipe walls
optionB: Groundwater pressure outside the pipe dissolves the crown from the outside inward
optionC: Hydrogen sulfide released above the waterline is converted to acid on the crown
optionD: Grease deposits floating on the surface protect the crown and attack the walls

Ask residents upstream to reduce water use during the next forecast storm event

question: Two parallel force mains serve one station. With one main out for inspection, peak flows exceed the safe velocity in the remaining main. Which long term fix fits?
correctAnswer: Stage renewal so firm capacity with one main out of service still meets peak flow
explanation: Planning firm capacity with one main out of service is the standard the situation calls for. Higher velocity, accepted shortfalls, and downstream storage do not fix the constraint.
options: Stage renewal so firm capacity with one main out of service still meets peak flow
Run the station pumps faster during peaks and accept the higher velocity in the main
Accept the shortfall, because inspections of the second main happen only rarely
Add storage at the treatment plant and leave the force main arrangement unchanged

question: Sulfide control dosing is optimized at one station, yet corrosion appears in a trunk about two kilometres downstream. Which factor best explains the gap?
correctAnswer: Long detention and warm sewage downstream let sulfide regenerate after dosing ends
explanation: Dosing effects fade with distance, and long warm detention downstream allows sulfide to form again. The corrosion pattern follows that regeneration, not excess residual.
options: The chemical dose was too effective, so the sewage arrived carrying excess residual
Gravity flow in the trunk removes sulfide faster than the force main can produce it
Long detention and warm sewage downstream let sulfide regenerate after dosing ends
Corrosion downstream is unrelated to sulfide whenever dosing is in place upstream

question: A utility must choose between storage and conveyance upgrades for a surcharging trunk. Flow data show the peaks are short but intense. Which option does that pattern favour?

Smaller pumps at the upstream station to slow the flow entering the trunk sewer
Deeper manholes along the route so the surcharge stays below the street surface

Coat the outside of the exposed pipe at the chambers and return the main to service
